content: I have been exploring how to visualise the connections between different areas of mathematics within Lean libraries. This led to *First Light*, a visualisation of the structure and dependencies across Mathlib4 and PhysLean I thought I would share the video here and would be interested in any feedback.
Hi Philip, is your code public? I'd love to take a look at how you made this.

Code is not currently public. I have built a queryable interface into Lean's meta-engine, created distance functions between different artefacts then built a native mac rendering to enable exploring mathematics in an interactive way.

// ── The fourth dimension of the Mathematics Observatory ─────────────
─────────
// The Hypersphere projection lifts each node off the globe (its S² embedding)
// into a fourth spatial dimension — by how far its formal domain sits from the
// foundations — placing the whole corpus on a 4-sphere, then turns it with a
// double rotation. Foundations live on the invariant w≈0 axis, so mathematics
// visibly rotates around its logical core. The Globe projection is exactly
// this object's w = 0 shadow: same data, one dimension down.
//
// Everything here is pure geometry over data the Rust engine already supplies
// (coordinates.sphere_x/y/z and domain). No engine change is required.
